paperTitle: O-Level Basic Band — Practice 06: The Umbrella
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band. Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Target: students who score only a few marks on the full O-Level band. Short passage (~230 words, everyday vocabulary), 2 short-answer + 3 MCQ. The 3:2 split is grounded in real data — typed items run a 64% blank rate in the weakest cohort, so most marks must be reachable by choosing.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
It rained every afternoon that week. I never brought an umbrella, because the sky was always blue at seven in the morning.

Paragraph 2
On Thursday the rain came down hard just as school ended. I stood under the covered walkway with about twenty other students and waited.

Paragraph 3
After ten minutes most of them had gone. Their parents came, or their friends shared umbrellas with them.

Paragraph 4
An old man was sweeping the walkway near me. He had been there all week. I had never spoken to him.

Paragraph 5
He stopped sweeping and looked at the rain. Then he walked to a corner, picked up a blue umbrella, and held it out to me.

Paragraph 6
'Take it,' he said. 'Someone left it here in May. Nobody came back for it.'

Paragraph 7
I said I could not take it. He pushed it into my hand and went back to his sweeping.

Paragraph 8
The next morning I brought the umbrella back. He was not there. He was not there on Monday either. A woman cleaning the toilets told me he only worked until the end of the month.

Paragraph 9
I still have the blue umbrella. It is in my bag every day now, even when the sky is clear.

questions.stem: Q1. From Paragraph 5, what colour was the umbrella? [1]
Q2. From Paragraph 8, who told the writer about the old man? [1]

questions.stem: Q3. Why did the writer never bring an umbrella? [1]

options.text: She liked walking in the rain.

questions.stem: Q4. In Paragraph 6, why did the old man think he could give the umbrella away? [1]

options.text: The school told him to give it away.
It had been lost for months and no one claimed it.
It was broken and no longer useful.

questions.stem: Q5. In Paragraph 9, why does the writer carry the umbrella even on clear days? [1]

options.text: She is afraid of getting wet.
She wants to return it to him one day.
It reminds her of the old man's kindness.
Her mother told her to take it.
